svg.text: PR #2209 · Add a production self-hosting stack and guide
Self-hosting meant a dev compose with sample secrets and a published Postgres port.
deploy/ now runs a pinned image behind Caddy HTTPS with generated secrets and backups.
BEFORE
AFTER
docker-compose.yml: a development stack
Builds from source, publishes db on 5432, ships
dev_password and a localhost OAuth callback;
no TLS, no backups, Google described as required.
container.yml tags :short_sha and :latest
Nothing ties an image to the version the portal
reports, so there is no sane pin.
Image /data/archive owned by root
The backend runs as appuser (1001): a mounted local
archive volume could not be written.
deploy/compose.yaml + Caddyfile + setup.sh
db on an internal network, only Caddy on 80/443 with
automatic Let's Encrypt; setup.sh writes .env (600) with
generated secrets and prints the exact callback URL.
Also tags :major.minor.commit-count
Same string as /api/health; compose pins it via
PORTAL_VERSION, so up -d never upgrades by surprise.
Dockerfile chowns /data; backup.sh / restore.sh
pg_dump + archive tarball; restore swaps both and
restarts. Round trip verified locally; documented in
docs/SELF_HOSTING.md with upgrade and rollback.
Single-host only. Wildcard TLS for port forwarding is documented, not automated; launchers still self-update from GitHub, not the portal's version.
